summary: Joe Arpaio, a former federal narcotics agent, served as sheriff of Maricopa County, Arizona, from 1993 to 2016, running a deadly tent jail, staging media stunts, and leading racial-profiling immigration sweeps until a contempt conviction.

evidence.note: born 1932 in Springfield, Massachusetts, to Italian immigrant parents
joins the Federal Bureau of Narcotics; undercover drug work begins
posted to Istanbul in 1961; opium bust and disputed Turkish gunfight stories
Operation Intercept border blockade, then Mexico City posting
1992 sheriff election; takes office the following January
tent jail, deprivations and chain gangs built for press coverage
1996 death of Scott Norberg in a restraint chair, injuries described
2006 pivot to targeting immigrants with smuggling law and posse sweeps
PR aide Lisa Allen engineering viral stunts such as pink underwear
inmate's late-term stillbirth after medical neglect in the tent jail
profiling suit, ignored injunction, 2017 contempt conviction and pardon
loses 2016 reelection, 2018 Senate bid and 2020 sheriff primary

notes: Arpaio was alive at release (2021), so covered_span runs to 2021 under the lifetime rule. main_span ends at the 2017 conviction and pardon rather than his 2016 ouster. Turkey and Mexico have real segments from his narcotics career. A posse prostitution sting with sexual coercion of sex workers gets a few minutes; sexual-violence warning left off as borderline.
